tracks.narration: Whirl a ball around at constant speed — same speed, curved path, and it is still accelerating. How?
A ball moving in a circle keeps turning. Even at constant speed, the velocity vector keeps changing direction — and a change in velocity is acceleration.
That acceleration always points inward, toward the centre of the circle. Its size is the speed squared divided by the radius.
Substitute v equals r omega, and the same acceleration becomes r omega squared.
Centripetal acceleration sits perpendicular to the motion at every instant — so it does no work. It does not speed the ball up. It just steers.
